evidence.title: Outside of Little Rock, Arkansas counties and cities move ahead on data center moratoriums
evidence.supports: Confirms the county's wind-turbine ban is a separate, pre-existing October 2025 instrument, cited only as context/trigger for the 2026 data-center ordinance.
evidence.quote: The county passed a three-year ban on wind turbines in October 2025 — only to find out about two months ago that a company had dozens of contracts to build turbines that predated the court's measure

evidence.title: Independence County Quorum Court places 5-year moratorium on data centers
evidence.supports: Confirms Ordinance No. 2026-21 is titled and scoped to commercial data centers only.

decisions.notes: SECTOR_CHECK: 'wind' refers to Independence County's separate, already-existing October 2025 wind-turbine moratorium, cited only as background/trigger context for the 2026 data-center ordinance, not as part of its operative scope. sectors correctly remains ["data_center"].

evidence.title: Council adopts six-month moratorium on data centers, creates ad hoc committee to draft regulations
evidence.supports: Confirms the Council amended the sponsor's original 18-month proposal down to six months before adopting it, i.e. six months (180 days) is the actual enacted/original term, and 18 months was an earlier, un-adopted proposal.

evidence.title: Data centers placed on buffering mode by Russellville Council
evidence.supports: Confirms the council amended and adopted a six-month (not 18-month) moratorium on July 16, 2026.

decisions.notes: DURATION_MISMATCH: duration_days=180 already correctly reflects the ORIGINAL (and only) adopted term of six months. The 18-month figure in the duration text is an earlier councilmember proposal that the Council amended down (6-2) before adoption, not a separate/later instrument, so per process guidance the typed value is left unchanged.
